sections.title: Announcement returns
sections.question: How does the stock react when the board removes the CEO?
sections.interpretation: Over the three trading days around the announcement, forced exits earn a market-model abnormal return of -1.6% (p <0.001), while voluntary retirements earn -0.1% (p 0.329). The gap is -1.5 percentage points (p <0.001). When the CEO removed is the founder, the three-day abnormal return is -3.5%, against -1.5% for non-founders, a gap of -2.0 percentage points (p 0.139). In a regression with event-year effects the founder interaction is -1.8 percentage points (p 0.181). Dismissals for conduct earn -4.0% against -1.3% for performance dismissals, a gap of -2.7 percentage points (p 0.003). The 17 removals that followed a relationship with an employee average -2.6% (p 0.103).

methodology.test: Cross-sectional t, Boehmer-Musumeci-Poulsen standardized t, Wilcoxon signed-rank; Welch t for differences
methodology.data: Daily total returns (Sharadar closeadj), market model estimated over days -250 to -30
methodology.caveat: Day 0 is the first trading day on or after the announcement.

sections.title: Long-run returns
sections.question: Does the firm do better or worse in the years after the removal?
sections.interpretation: Against the market, the median forced-exit firm's three-year buy-and-hold abnormal return is -18.4%. Against a matched firm in the same industry with similar size and profitability, the median is -2.7% (p 0.489), and the forced-minus-retired difference is -1.8 percentage points (p 0.603).

methodology.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank; skewness-adjusted t with bootstrap CI (Lyon, Barber and Tsai 1999)
methodology.data: Buy-and-hold returns from day +2, delisting returns per Shumway (1997)
methodology.caveat: Market-adjusted BHARs are right-skewed; matched-firm BHARs are the main test.

tables.title: Table 2. Long-run returns and operating performance (medians)
tables.notes: Medians. BHAR vs market compounds from day +2 against the value-weighted market. Matched BHAR subtracts the buy-and-hold return of a control firm in the same Fama-French industry with market value within 30 percent and the closest operating ROA in the prior year. ROA is EBITDA over total assets from as-reported statements, winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles; changes are from year -1, measured against the control, in percentage points (pp). Delisted firms keep their final return.

sections.question: Does profitability change after the removal, relative to a matched firm?
sections.interpretation: In the first year after a forced exit, the median change in operating return on assets relative to the matched firm is -0.6 percentage points (p 0.037); by year three it is 0.0 percentage points (p 0.647).

methodology.data: Sharadar as-reported annual statements, EBITDA over total assets
methodology.caveat: Matched on industry, size within 70-130%, and pre-event ROA; no CEO turnover at the control within three years.

sections.title: Robustness
sections.question: Do the main results survive other models, samples and definitions?
sections.interpretation: With the five-factor model, the founder gap is -1.8 percentage points (p 0.220) and the conduct gap is -2.4 percentage points (p 0.008). Adding the 24 retirements our coding identifies as pushed out gives a forced-exit return of -1.5%. Excluding 2008 and 2009 gives -1.7%. Using only strict matches, the median three-year matched return is -2.3%.

methodology.test: as in sections C and D
methodology.data: as in sections C and D
methodology.caveat: Pushed retirements come from the model coding of the dataset notes and are not hand-checked.
